notes: Idol for LiteRT (litert-community/Idol main 4ce77622, last modified 2026-11-09T17:09:05.000Z): speridlabs/idol (Apache-2.0) with the speridlabs/idol-turbo LoRA (5 steps, no guidance) turns one photo of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat; this form makes 262,144 Gaussians (8,192 anchors, the author's default). It is the first release's form, in the repo's 262k/ folder since the two-form commit 74728e5c (its files are the bytes of the first release's root at commit e7ee1226); the repo's root holds the default form (65,536 Gaussians), whose records are model id idol. Raw LiteRT graphs exported with litert-torch: BiRefNet background removal (bir, CPU), the DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 image encoder (dino_0..3, in litert-community/DINOv3-ViT-H16plus-Idol-LiteRT main e7842b44, gated), the FLUX.2 VAE encoder (vae_0..3, vae_attn, vae_4), the denoiser (den_ctx, den_in, den_joint_00..23: a graph per joint block), the octree decoder (oct, 5 signatures by row count) and the Gaussian decoder (gs_0..7). A pipeline record: `artifact` is 262k/manifest.json, which the app opens; it names the 47 graphs with file, bytes, sha256, accelerator and GPU precision (FP16 with fp32 accumulation for the 46 GPU graphs, one of them the alternative matting graph dis, which lives in litert-community/DIS-ISNet-LiteRT and this run did not use). Identity: the sha256 in 262k/manifest.json of every graph the app loads equals its Hub LFS sha256 (the 42 graphs under 262k/ and the 4 DINOv3 graphs), 262k/manifest.json's git blob id and every side and JSON file equal the uploaded files, and the app's install script checks each file's SHA-256 on the phone. Lines, fixed before the first run: (a) each part against the author's PyTorch pipeline (float32, CPU) on the same input, cosine >= 0.99 per compared tensor; (b) the whole pipeline's 4-view render PSNR against the author's default >= 25 dB on three inputs (nb-armchair and fig-axolotl from the author's gallery, a Pexels photo of a succulent). A pipeline check, so output_match stays null and the scores are metrics; latency_p50_ms stays null and the photo walls are metrics (first_photo_wall_s is the conversion's published speed figure for this form on this phone). Harness: the same sample app as the default form's records (a debug build of the repo's android/ folder) in its autorun mode, pointed at the 262k/ files: the app starts, compiles 0 of its 45 GPU graphs before the photo, then makes one photo of nb-armchair from the app's files (plan e2e_cool, run 0; it compiles each graph during the photo). Before it the run waited for a cool phone: GPU clock cap 1,300 MHz and thermal status <= 1 in three reads 10 s apart (567 s of waiting; status 0 and skin 34.6 C at the photo's start). While the app ran the GPU clock cap fell to 500 MHz (thermal status 0 -> 2). The armchair .ply is byte-identical to the first release's app's, and this app's fig-axolotl .ply from the same graph bytes (an earlier device run the same night, whose manifest copy differed only in BiRefNet's memory estimate) is byte-identical to the first release's app's, so those two line (b) scores apply to this app. The metrics prefixed first_release_app_ come from the first release's app build on the same graph bytes: line (a) on this phone (its parity plan), the succulent's line (b), the first photo after start that the first release's card gives (from thermal status 1) and five photos on a phone already warm (thermal status 2: three of nb-armchair, then the succulent and fig-axolotl). Not rows here: this app's earlier photos of the same bytes (the device run named above; its first photo started at thermal status 1) and the other forms of the conversion's speed comparison. The Pixel 11 Pro did not time this form.
quantization: none: the graphs store float32 weights; every graph but BiRefNet runs on the GPU at GPU precision FP16 with fp32 accumulation, BiRefNet on the CPU in float32
